extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing/resubmitting an NIH R01 (PA-13-302) research application in AAV gene therapy
extracted.subtask_short: NIH R01 resubmission for AAV research
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare a resubmitted NIH R01 research application (PHS398) focused on adeno-associated virus (AAV) liver transduction and capsid immune evasion, including Specific Aims, Research Strategy, biosketches, budgets, human/animal subject sections, and point-by-point responses to prior reviewers' critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address prior reviewers' critiques in resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond point-by-point to reviewers' identified weaknesses (explicitly noted: 1) the approaches are not innovative and are likely to lead to only incremental progress, 2) the rationale for the experimental design was poorly articulated and 3) the applicants did not adequately consider the effect of pre-existing immune responses on antigen presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear Introduction that summarizes reviewer concerns and documents how each has been addressed (e.g., combining aims, adding new Aim 3, stronger rationale, additional experiments, removal of problematic models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims clarity and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims must state objectives, hypotheses and enumerate discrete aims and sub-aims (example structure: Aim 1a/1b/1c; Aim 2a/2b/2c; Aim 3a/3b/3c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each aim should be concise, testable, and linked to measurable outcomes; include sub-aims where appropriate and explicitly state how each aim contributes to the overall goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (clinical and conceptual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate the significance of the problem (e.g., AAV capsid-specific CTL elimination of transduced hepatocytes is an outstanding barrier to successful AAV liver gene therapy) and why the proposed work addresses an important gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain translational relevance and how findings will inform safer/more effective human liver gene therapy; cite clinical trials and prior work demonstrating the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (avoid incrementalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that approaches are innovative rather than only incremental (example: combine directed evolution with rational design to derive novel capsids that avoid ubiquitination and CTL recognition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state what is novel about the methods, constructs or conceptual advances compared with prior work and how innovation increases impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific rationale and experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide careful rationale linking observed data, hypotheses and experimental plans (reviewers noted rationale was previously poorly articulated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mechanistic reasoning, expected outcomes, and a 'pitfall and alternative approaches' section to show robustness and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data and established protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Document existing working protocols, assays and animal models that support feasibility (e.g., prior observations that capsid antigen presentation is dose-dependent and proteasome-dependent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite publications and include preliminary in vitro/in vivo data demonstrating assay performance and feasibility of planned experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate animal models and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and justify animal models suited to the questions (examples in text: TAP-/- and Cat S-/- mice; human hepatocyte xenograft mice); remove or revise models deemed inappropriate (HepG2/H2-Kb/TAP-/- was deleted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why each model is chosen, its limitations, and how results will translate to human biology; revise plans if reviewers identified inappropriate models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety considerations for viral vectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe biosafety measures for the use of AAV and adenoviral vectors (reviewer comment: biosafety consideration was not described and was later provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include containment level, institutional approvals (IACUC, IBC), safety procedures, and any risk mitigation relevant to vector use and human/animal subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of pre-existing immunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly address the impact of pre-existing antibody and cellular immunity on antigen presentation and feasibility of planned studies (e.g., pre-existing antibody blocks AAV transduction making certain assays infeasible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State limitations imposed by pre-existing immunity, how experiments account for it, and how proposed capsid modifications intend to overcome cellular immune responses independent of antibody status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanistic hypotheses about antigen presentation pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: State and test mechanistic models (e.g., classical class I presentation and cross-presentation, TAP-dependent/proteasome-dependent vs TAP-independent/protease-dependent pathways; role of ubiquitination and endosomal escape).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments to distinguish pathways (genetic knockouts, pharmacological inhibitors) and link mechanistic readouts to functional outcomes (transduction, CTL elimination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dose-response and kinetics analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Include studies of kinetics and dose-response for capsid antigen presentation from empty and full AAV particles in vivo (Aim 1a/1b), since antigen presentation is dose-dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify timepoints, doses, and quantitative readouts to capture both short-term and long-term antigen processing/presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay selection and control for construct effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether assay constructs (e.g., insertion of the OVA SIINFEKL peptide into capsid loops) affect biological function (transduction) and provide alternative assays if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a tagged/engineered assay alters transduction, employ alternative approaches such as peptide-specific CTLs induced by immunization, and discuss sensitivity trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proteasome inhibitor dosing and combinatorial strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that proteasome inhibitors (e.g., bortezomib) have dose-dependent effects: high dose can block presentation while low dose may increase presentation without enhancing transduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design dose-ranging experiments, analyze effects on both transduction efficiency and antigen presentation, and test combinations with AAV mutants for synergy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking study outcomes to ultimate translational goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly describe how the experimental outcomes (e.g., enhanced transduction, reduced capsid presentation, isolated human-tropic CTL-evading capsids) will achieve the overall goal of safer/effective AAV liver gene therapy and progression toward clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map each aim's output to translational milestones and possible next steps for clinical development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel justification and percent effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Personnel Justification detailing roles, percent effort (CM years), responsibilities for PI(s), co-investigators, postdocs, technicians, and fringe benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific tasks for each named individual, effort allocation by project year, and fringe benefit calculations per institutional policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget completeness and modular budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a modular budget for each budget period showing direct costs, consortium F&A, indirect costs with indirect cost rate and cognizant agency information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include budget justifications, consortium justification, and cumulative budget information; provide documentation of indirect cost rate agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 required sections/attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach required PHS 398 sections: Introduction (for resubmission), Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Progress Report Publication List, Protection of Human Subjects, Inclusion of Women and Minorities, Inclusion of Children, Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan, Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plan(s), Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide each section as a separate PDF as indicated by the form and ensure human/animal subject sections are complete if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research support disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: List ongoing and pending research support (grant numbers, role, period) and describe how proposed work relates (e.g., R01DK084033, R01 AI072176, P01HL112761, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify overlap/duplciation of effort, show feasibility and capability without unacceptable overlap, and indicate MPI/subPI roles where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing and data/materials availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Resource Sharing Plan(s) describing how data, vectors, materials, and other resources will be shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include links or documents (e.g., ResourceSharingPlan1022072245.pdf) and specify timelines and conditions for sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch content and contributions to science
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a biosketch with Personal Statement, Positions and Honors, and 'Contributions to Science' describing major contributions with citation support (including a MyBibliography link).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight relevant expertise, leadership, prior discoveries, key publications, and examples of translational or clinical impact.
